key_insight: Ranking-preserving coresets accelerate evolutionary hyperparameter optimization by evaluating configurations on compact data subsets designed to preserve full-data performance rankings.
engineering_relevance: Reusing a selected coreset can reduce repeated model-training costs while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-data optimization.
method: Evolve a coreset to maximize Spearman correlation between subset-based and full-data configuration rankings.
Penalize subset size to balance ranking fidelity against computational cost.
Run hyperparameter optimization on the coreset using GA, CHC, or PSO.
evidence_signal: Across 11 tabular, text, and image datasets, HPO-stage speedups were approximately 1.14×–8.80×; on 20 held-out configurations, ranking correlation exceeded same-size random sampling on 8 datasets (Wilcoxon p = 0.014).
watch_item: HPO-stage speedups exclude one-time coreset construction; assess end-to-end runtime and the number of reuse runs needed to break even.
paper_title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
